name: PPS pivotal trials
question: Does oral pentosan polysulfate sodium improve interstitial cystitis symptoms more than placebo?

design.population: 110 patients with at least one year of interstitial cystitis, at least 10 voids/day and 2/night, cystoscopic findings, and prior unsuccessful conventional treatment enrolled at five centers.
design.locator: Full text, Material and Methods, p 553; Results, p 555

verdictNote: Patient-rated global improvement met the study's P ≤ 0.05 threshold at three months.
takeaway: In the three-month Mulholland trial (54 assigned pentosan polysulfate sodium; 56 placebo), patient-reported global improvement greater than 25% occurred in 28% versus 13% (15-percentage-point difference from rounded rates; P = 0.04).

reports.label: Mulholland placebo-controlled trial
reports.citation: Mulholland SG, Hanno P, Parsons CL, et al. "Pentosan polysulfate sodium for therapy of interstitial cystitis. A double-blind placebo-controlled clinical study." *Urology.* 1990;35(6):552-558. doi:10.1016/0090-4295(90)80116-5
reports.followUpLocator: Full text, Material and Methods, pp 553–554

results.measure: Greater than 25% overall improvement at 3 months; risk difference in percentage points
results.note: Risk difference calculated from rounded percentages. The report gives 54 and 56 assigned but no endpoint-specific denominators or confidence interval. Results text on p 555 gives 18% for placebo, conflicting with Table II, abstract, and discussion (13%).
results.locator: Full text, Table II, p 556; Comment, p 557

results.note: Risk difference calculated from rounded percentages. The report gives 54 and 56 assigned but no endpoint-specific denominators or confidence interval.
